targets.name: ESP32 (ESP-IDF)
targets.build_notes:
Before the first build, set the Wi-Fi network with `idf.py menuconfig`, under **IoT OS
application**. `sdkconfig` keeps the password, and `.gitignore` keeps it out of version
control. The project builds for the ESP32; for another chip, such as the ESP32-S3 or
ESP32-C3, first run `idf.py set-target esp32s3` with that chip's name. The SDK brings its
own MQTT client, so do not add the coreMQTT component from the ESP Component Registry,
whose symbols clash with it, and do not connect to the platform with ESP-IDF's MQTT
client.

targets.name: NXP i.MX RT1050 (MCUXpresso SDK)
targets.build_notes:
Before the first build, fetch the MCUXpresso SDK 26.09.00, which is not included (about
2 GB for this board), and point the build at it and at the Arm GNU Toolchain:

```sh
west init -m https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcuxsdk-manifests --mr v26.09.00 mcuxsdk-26.09
cd mcuxsdk-26.09
west update --narrow -o=--depth=1 core CMSIS mcux-devices-rt mcu-sdk-examples mcu-sdk-components \
  mcuxsdk-tool-data lwip mbedtls3x freertos-kernel freertos-kernel-upstream mcux-freertos-drivers
export MCUXSDK_ROOT="$PWD/mcuxsdk" ARMGCC_DIR=/path/to/arm-gnu-toolchain-14.2.rel1
```

The build finds the SDK only through `MCUXSDK_ROOT` and the toolchain through `ARMGCC_DIR`,
so set both in every shell that builds. The project is for the MIMXRT1050-EVKB over Ethernet: its pins, clocks and PHY are in
`board/`, and the SDK components it uses are in `prj.conf`. Code runs from the board's flash
and data from its SDRAM. A gateway also polls Modbus RTU devices over RS-485 on LPUART3, in
`app/modbus_rtu.c`. Flash with LinkServer through the board's debug USB port, or with a
J-Link. The SDK brings its own MQTT client, so leave the MCUXpresso coreMQTT middleware
unselected: two copies give duplicate symbols.
